description:
FILED s407 (Fable) â docs/option-b-phase2-plan.md Â§2 Track A is the spec.  The
s407 drop harvest (tools/drop-harvest.pl over the census) shows ~300 of the 373
census drops are FEATURE ABSENCES or deliberate error tests, not parser gaps.
At the two PARSE-ERROR emitters in Pl/Parser.pm (where _announce_dropped_
statement is called), classify the LEADING shape of the dropped statement and
DIE perl-shaped with a not-supported.md entry:
  given/when/default (+ CORE::given)  -> "PCL: given/when (feature 'switch') is not supported â removed in perl 5.42"
  class/field/method/ADJUST           -> "PCL: feature 'class' is not supported"   (method: only with a class block open or feature 'class' in scope â a Moose-style `method` sub name must not be misdiagnosed; the die fires ONLY at a drop site anyway)
  format NAME =                       -> cite the existing formats entry
  infix ~~                            -> "PCL: smartmatch (~~) is not supported â removed in perl 5.42"
  indirect object WORD $obj LIST      -> "PCL: indirect object syntax is not supported"
  defer {                             -> "PCL: defer blocks are not supported" (until implemented â Track C)
  lvalue-sub assignment               -> UNCHANGED: stays a loud drop (fable-answers-s400 Â§6.3)
Everything else keeps dropping (announced) until Track B / the flip.
BOUNDARY: this runs only where a statement was ALREADY lost â it cannot break
compiling code; the keywords are perl CORE features (language; 9a's smell test
is about CPAN modules).
BAR: census falls by exactly the families' counts, no other row moves
(tools/drop-census.pl before/after, census edited row by row with the cause);
companion: op/switch.t, class/*.t, smartmatch.t register XDIFF with the entry;
sweep TOTAL/LOST â a die where a drop was may abort a file EARLIER
(perl-tests/state.t has one `given`): if a file loses passing rows, its rows
are re-blessed ROW BY ROW with the cause, never a blanket re-bless; gate.


IMPLEMENTED s415 -- with TWO of the seven table rows changed by the measurement.

SHIPPED: one classifier, Pl::Parser::_ruled_refusal_for_drop, asked by
_announce_dropped_statement (which both PARSE-ERROR emitters already call), so
it runs ONLY where a statement was already lost.  Five families die
perl-shaped, each citing docs/not-supported.md: given/when/default (+CORE::),
class/field/method/ADJUST, an uncaught `format NAME =`, `defer {`, and INFIX
`~~`.  Guard: Pl/t/ruled-refusal-01.t, 27 rows in 1 s, every refusing shape
paired with the sibling that must keep dropping.

CONSERVATIVE BY CONSTRUCTION (a miss costs nothing, a false positive costs a
file): `~~` only with a TERM before it (`is(~~$y, 3)` in bop.t, 507 rows, is a
double complement and PPI lexes both as one token); field/method/ADJUST only
when the FILE says feature 'class' is on, with no shape guard beside it (PPI
reads `method m { 1 }` as a m{...} MATCH).

CHANGED BY MEASUREMENT (tools/drop-harvest.pl over the census):
 * INDIRECT OBJECT removed from the list -> task #399.  Its only two drops are
   perl-tests/ref.t:334 and method.t:72, files with 191 and 97 passing rows;
   ~288 rows to convert 2 drops, and perl still parses the syntax.
 * FORMAT inverted: the drops were in PRODUCTIVE files (t/op/closure.t has 267
   passing rows), so the MECHANISM was fixed.  The source-level stripper's
   `($str_re)|` pass-through is defeated by any quote imbalance (a `"` inside a
   regex, an apostrophe pair across two comments, a quote in a picture line):
   t/op/write.t stripped 39 of its 104 formats and the 65 survivors each ate
   the next statement.  It is now line-anchored (_strip_format_blocks), the
   name may be anything up to the `=`, and removed lines become EMPTY lines so
   later line numbers match perl's.  The shared skip pattern now also consumes
   comments, which fixed two more silent wrongs: the HEX-FLOAT pass was
   rewriting hex-float text inside string literals (sprintf2.t's EXPECTATIONS
   became "-0"), and `CORE::state $x = 42` was not normalised.

BAR MET: gate 151 files / 5550 rows (only the 13 pclxs xs rows); corpus-diff 4
of 111 files, each explained (state.t the refusal, sprintf2.t + sub.t the two
fixes, ref.t p-die line numbers now perl's); full sweep GATE clean, 0 new, 5
fixed, TOTAL 18367; drop census 73 files / 378 drops -> 56 / 177, no file's
count up because of this change (the two "new" census rows measure 1 at HEAD
too -- the census was stale for them).

COST, recorded in task #400 and in both baselines BY HAND: perl-tests/state.t
158 -> 0 and t/op/state.t 126 -> 0, one `given` block each.  Everything else
the five families touch was already producing 0-27 rows.
